title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-16
content:
Security Engineering Weekly Sync - 2026-03-16
Attendees: Ethan Chen (owner), Aisha Kapoor, Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Neill, Priya Rao, + ad-hoc from ENG infra (Sam), SRE (Jules)
Absentees: N/A

Agenda:
- Quick wins & action item review
- Vulnerability triage (public CVEs + internal findings)
- Secrets scanning and rotating expired tokens
- Threat modeling: dedicated routing feature (RFC-in-flight)
- AOB / blockers

Notes / Decisions:
1) Quick wins / Action item review\- SEC-3421 (k8s node auth hardening): Aisha confirms PR merged last week; rollout to staging completed 2026-03-12. Remaining: prod rollout window needs approval from infra for 2026-03-19. ACTION: Aisha to schedule prod rollout and post-runbook to Confluence.\- Secrets policy doc (draft): Sofia updated guidance on short-lived tokens; feedback requested by EOD Friday. ACTION: Team to add any remaining OSS integration notes.

2) Vulnerability triage\- Public CVE intake: we received automated alert for CVE-2026-1457 (grpc-java dependency) flagged by Dependabot. Impact: runtime ingestion workers in Dedicated clusters use grpc-java v1.48 in some older stacks. Initial assessment: low exploitability without lateral access, but needs upgrade. ACTION: Liam to open SEC ticket and test upgrade path in canary. Ticket: SEC-3499.\- Internal finding: Snyk flagged a file-include pattern in one of the internal helm charts that could expose metadata if misconfigured. Severity: medium. Mitigation: update chart defaults and add a post-install check. ACTION: Priya to create PR with chart defaults + CI check (due 2026-03-18).\- Prioritization: we agreed to follow: critical public CVEs > high internal findings affecting prod surface > medium > low. For medium items, add guardrails (monitoring / compensating controls) until patch is available.

3) Secrets scanning + rotations\- Overview: periodic scan found 3 expired-ish service tokens embedded in old-sample-app repo. Two are already rotated; one still present (samples/auth-mock/testdata). ACTION: Ethan to coordinate with owner (DevX) to remove sample token and replace with ephemeral fixture before EOD 2026-03-17.\- Vault migration status: migration of service accounts to Vault dynamic secrets is 70% complete for hosted infra. Current blockers: legacy CI jobs still use static tokens. ACTION: Sofia to run a sweep of CI jobs and list remaining static-token consumers by 2026-03-19.\- Secrets policy update: draft recommends max 7-day TTL for CI ephemeral tokens, mandatory scanning on PRs touching infra/ops folders. Team agreed to require two approvals for any PR disabling scanning.

4) Threat modeling - dedicated routing feature (RFC #1256)\- Summary: product wants per-customer routing policies that can prefer cheaper model variants or fall back to regional pools. Potential threats discussed: policy injection (malicious routing rules), information leakage via routing metadata, DoS amplification by creating heavy fan-out routing, privilege escalation from routing config UI.\- Key mitigations agreed:\  - Config validation & allowlist: only validated routing constructs shipped; deny unknown policy patterns.\  - RBAC: restrict who can create/modify routing policies (product-admin, infra-admin roles).\  - Audit logging: every routing decision must log inputs (policy id, model variant used, request id) with redaction of PII.\  - Rate limiting + circuit breaker: prevent fan-out exceeding X (TBD) for new policies until warmed.\- Open questions:\  - Do we allow customer-supplied JS transforms for routing? (Short answer: no \u2014 too risky). ACTION: Ethan to add explicit ban to RFC and draft enforcement approach.\  - Telemetry retention for audit logs: retention 90d by default, longer for enterprise only. ACTION: Security to propose retention policy by next sync (2026-03-23).

5) Operational notes / monitoring\- Canary testing: runtime PR #1228 (improved kv-cache eviction logic) is in canary; no regressions observed for token-level latency. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1228. ACTION: Jules to monitor canary for 72h and report.\- Incident playbook refresh: discussed adding a quick-check checklist for vuln disclosure (who to notify, external comms templates). ACTION: Priya to draft and share for review (due 2026-03-20).

6) Blockers / Risks\- Infra capacity for rolling CVE patches: infra has limited maintenance windows in Dedicated clusters. Need to coordinate with sales/ops for customer impact windows. ACTION: Aisha to sync with Customer Success on 2026-03-17.\- Secrets scanning false positives causing PR friction: agreed to improve scanning rules and provide an easy override with justification that auto-creates an issue for remediation. ACTION: Sofia + DevX to propose override UX.

7) Action items (summary)\- Aisha Kapoor: schedule prod rollout for SEC-3421 (due 2026-03-19) + sync with Customer Success.\- Liam O'Neill: open SEC-3499 (grpc-java upgrade) + test canary upgrade (due 2026-03-18).\- Priya Rao: PR for helm chart defaults + CI check and incident/vuln disclosure playbook draft (PR due 2026-03-18; playbook due 2026-03-20).\- Ethan Chen: remove sample token from samples repo (due 2026-03-17); add ban on customer-supplied transforms to RFC #1256.\- Sofia Martinez: CI static-token sweep and secrets scanning override UX proposal (due 2026-03-19).\- Jules (SRE): monitor runtime PR canary for 72h and report.

Notes to self / rough thoughts:\- Consider a "routing policy linter" that runs at policy-creation time to catch risky fan-out patterns.\- Evaluate retention and indexing cost for audit logs; may need tiered storage.

Next meeting: 2026-03-23 10:00 PT (weekly)
If urgent issues arise (critical CVE or active compromise) we will spin up ad-hoc incident call.

Links / references: Confluence Weekly: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Security+Weekly+Sync, Tickets: SEC-3421, SEC-3499, Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1228

End of notes.
